title: Honey Bottle, Cap & Delivered-Cost Review
imageCaption: Honey bottle samples, matching caps and protective carton planning.
summary: A honey bottle sourcing project comparing existing-cap compatibility, complete-pack options and delivered cost.
facts: Existing lid versus a complete new pack
Proposed bottle option exceeded the budget
sections: Project Requirements
A honey business approached Gracepack for bottles to use with caps already purchased locally. The project required a suitable honey fill size, confirmation of cap fit and a shipping-volume estimate.
Honey Weight & Bottle Capacity

The initial discussion clarified honey net weight and container volume before bottle selection. A weight in grams does not translate directly to the same number of milliliters; the actual honey and fill line determine the required capacity.
Existing Cap Compatibility

The team asked about the existing cap and whether the proposed bottle neck would fit it. Later exchanges compared a bottle-only route with a complete bottle-and-cap route, including a valve-cap option. Similar-looking lids were not treated as proof of compatibility.
Bottle, Closure & Delivery Costs
The quotation compared local consolidation and delivery options alongside bottle and closure costs. Compatibility with the existing cap still required sample testing before approval.
Quotation Outcome
The proposed bottle route exceeded the project budget. The project remained at quotation stage, with no bottle production order confirmed.
Preparing a Bottle & Cap Quotation

Send the target honey net weight, a drawing or sample of any existing cap, the order quantity and destination together. Ask for bottle-only and complete-pack quotations where relevant, and confirm the physical assembly before choosing a route.

title: 250 ml vs. 320 ml Honey Bear Bottles
imageCaption: 250 ml and 320 ml honey bear bottle size comparison.
summary: Compare 250 ml and 320 ml bear bottles for two branded honey pack sizes.
sections: Honey Pack Size Selection
Choose the intended honey net weight before finalizing the bottle and label. The 250 ml and 320 ml bear formats provide two starting points for a coordinated product range.
Reference Honey Fill & Headspace
The 250 ml bear has an approximate 350 g honey fill, while the 320 ml bear has an approximate 450 g fill. Confirm the packed weight and headspace with your honey and agreed fill line.
Front Label Dimensions

Both formats leave the molded bear shape visible around a front label area. A consistent brand design can be adapted across the two sizes, but the label dimensions should be checked separately. A larger label scaled down on screen is not a substitute for an actual-size proof on the smaller bear.
Closure Fit & Packing Requirements
Both bottles list a 38-400 neck finish. Confirm each cap, liner and seal on the complete assembly, then test opening, grip and resealing with your honey.
Sample Evaluation & Packing Data
Select your target honey net weight, compare samples and proof the label on each body. Request the current packing list for each size before estimating shipping volume.
Specifications for a Bulk Quotation
Approve the bottle, closure, label and actual fill together. Include the selected size, quantity, destination and packing requirements in your quotation request.

title: Mini Glass Honey Jar Gift Packaging
imageCaption: Mini glass honey jars arranged with matching lids and gift-pack components.
summary: Plan a 25 ml round glass honey jar with its metal lid, label and protective gift-box insert.
sections: Jar, Lid & Gift-Box Selection
A 25 ml round glass jar provides a compact starting point for a honey gift. Coordinate the honey fill, lid, label and box insert to create the finished presentation.
Assembled Dimensions & Insert Clearance

The jar’s reference dimensions are 40.5 mm overall height with cap and 40 mm body diameter. Size the protective insert around the approved assembled sample, allowing space for easy removal and transit protection.
Small-Jar Labeling
Check the front label at its actual printed size. A lid sticker or outer-box panel provides additional space for your branding and required product information.
Lid & Filling-Process Approval
A metal cap option is available. Confirm the liner, seal and filling-temperature limits for the complete jar-and-lid assembly before production.
Carton Quantities & Glass Protection
The standard carton reference is 280 jars. Gift boxes and protective inserts change the packing volume, so request a separate packing and freight quotation for the finished gift configuration.
Gift Packaging Quotation Requirements
Share the jar quantity, lid finish, artwork, gift-box layout and delivery destination. Confirm which components are included and approve the assembled pack before production.
